chapter: Opinions on pop music, jazz education and the business
title: Where young players learn: Berklee and the old Harlem sessions
summary: Wilson and Hinton compare school big bands with the 25 Harlem bars of old where young players could sit in and improvise.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Well, the difference is there are no schools for these -- well, when I say 'schools' -- there are no places for young people to play like you said, where $e$even could go where they could sit in and play and get the exercise of improvising. Now you can go to school and read, and ..
Well, he does -- at Berklee College, they have it. That's part of their work, big band playing and
five piece quintets; they have to read the parts in section playing, and play in combos, too. It's part of the work they do there.
That's good, because there aren't enough of them.

Yeah, like I say -- but that's just one school, where years ago, in Harlem, in one night you could go to 25 bars where that would be going on., like Minton's or like Monroe's Uptown House, where you would find all the top piano players up at Jimmy's Chicken Shack or someplace.
Or the Shalimar or some of those places on Broadway, or Wells.

Especially most of the colleges, academics and reading -- there are some excellent big bands as an ensemble, but most of the soloists were lacking because they probably hadn't had the experience of playing where you could just really blow.
